label: copy-phase input o (or m) late in recall, esp. when outputting o/z
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or on <DEL>), and almost only when the fed-back input is o (82% of mass) or m (17%). Mostly late in the recall (recall_idx >= 4, to_go <= 3; t 11-16), more often for L=9. Every active step is a repeat of a token seen earlier, which holds for any copy-phase input. Within o/m copy inputs, it is several times more likely when the token being output is z or o (then m, l, 3, j). The strongest activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max) are o inputs that output z or o. The token class alone gives high recall (o/m with recall_idx>=4: 93% mass recall) but very low precision (~3%), since most o/m copy steps stay inactive. Adding out_tok in {o,z} raises precision to ~36% but loses half the mass. I found no history variable (in_count, n_digits, to_go, prev tokens) that cleanly separates active from inactive o-input steps. Does not fire on other input tokens (apart from a handful of x/z/b/v).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=m (+5.95), phase=2 & in_tok=o (+4.87), in_tok=o (+3.03), phase=2 & out_tok=m (+2.95), phase=2 & out_tok=l (+2.74), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+2.46). Lower it: next_out=y (-2.89), prev_tok=2 (-2.61), prev_tok=1 (-2.58), orig5=- (-2.33).
